issues.legal_issue: The 1937 property-rights regime did not govern succession to the deceased family members’ interests because it was extended to their former state only after their deaths.
material_facts: The deceased family members died while the family resided in the erstwhile Hyderabad State.
The 1937 Act was made applicable to that state after their deaths.
issues.conclusion: The High Court erred in holding that the 1937 Act applied to the parties; it did not govern succession to the deceased members’ interests.
issues.legal_principle: The applicable succession regime is determined by the law in force when the relevant deaths occurred. The 1937 Act did not apply to the parties at those deaths because it was extended to the erstwhile Hyderabad State only later. No earlier cases are relied on for this conclusion.

predicates.inheritance_dispute: The proceeding concerns succession to family property after the deaths of family members.
predicates.relevant_deaths_preceded_local_extension: The family members whose interests are in issue died before the property-rights regime was extended to the territory where they resided.

issues.definition: When an inheritance dispute concerns deaths preceding the local extension of a property-rights regime, that later-extended regime does not govern succession.

issues.legal_issue: An adoption into a joint family does not divest a person of an estate vested before the adoption when the property remains held by the joint family and no individual estate has vested.
material_facts: The widows adopted children after their husbands had died.
The adopted children claimed shares in the joint family properties.
The 1937 Act did not apply at the husbands’ deaths.
The court found that the joint family continued to hold the property and that survivorship did not involve vesting or divesting an estate in the sense relevant to the statutory restriction.
issues.conclusion: The statutory restriction on divesting a person of an estate vested before adoption did not bar the adopted children from claiming shares in the joint family properties.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 12 of the Hindu Adoption and Maintenance Act, 1956, an adopted child is treated as a child of the adoptive family, subject to proviso (c), which prevents the child from divesting a person of an estate vested before the adoption. The entry of a member into a joint family may reduce the shares of other members but does not itself vest or divest the joint family estate. Devolution by survivorship on a member’s death is not vesting or divesting in the sense contemplated by proviso (c). No earlier cases are relied on.

predicates.adoption_in_joint_family_inheritance_dis: The proceeding concerns an adopted child’s claim to property held by a joint family.
predicates.property_remained_jointly_held: The family property continued to be held by the joint family after a member’s death and the adoption.
predicates.no_individual_estate_vested_before_adopt: No individual member had obtained a vested estate in the property before the adoption.

issues.definition: If an adopted child claims in a joint-family inheritance dispute and the property remained jointly held without an individual estate vesting before adoption, the child may claim a share in the joint-family property.

issues.legal_issue: An alleged partition that was not put in issue and was supported by scant evidence and no produced partition document was not established.
material_facts: The defendants alleged that a partition had taken place.
The partition question was not put in issue.
The evidence of partition was scanty, and neither the alleged partition deed nor a copy of the partition memorandum was produced.
The defendant who testified had not called on the person said to hold the deed to produce it.
The evidence did not explain why or how the partition was effected, including while the relevant sons were minors.
issues.conclusion: The High Court was justified in finding the alleged partition untenable.
issues.legal_principle: A claimed partition must be established by the evidence in the case. The absence of an issue on partition and the failure to produce the alleged partition documents, together with scant evidence and no adequate explanation of the partition, supported the finding that it was not established. No earlier cases are relied on.

rule.if: partition_dispute_in_inheritance_suit and partition_was_not_put_in_issue and partition_document_was_not_produced and partition_evidence_was_scant

predicates.partition_dispute_in_inheritance_suit: The proceeding concerns an inheritance claim in which a party alleges that the family property was partitioned.
predicates.partition_was_not_put_in_issue: The alleged partition was not made an issue for determination in the proceeding.
predicates.partition_document_was_not_produced: The party relying on the alleged partition did not produce the partition document said to exist.
predicates.partition_evidence_was_scant: The evidence did not adequately establish who effected the partition or the circumstances in which it occurred.

issues.definition: In an inheritance suit, an alleged partition is not established when it was not put in issue, the claimed partition document was not produced, and the supporting evidence was scant.
